query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing the conventional EAM reference with a machine‐learning potential (MLP) trained on ab initio data that encompass both solid and liquid configurations of the high-entropy alloy will improve the phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems, thereby reducing the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch compared to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: A multicomponent high-entropy alloy in both its solid state and in the fully molten liquid state near and at its high melting temperature.
generation.intervention: Substitute the EAM potential used in thermodynamic integration with a neural network-based or similar machine-learning potential that is explicitly trained on ab initio configurations representing the diverse atomic environments in both the solid and liquid phases.
generation.conditions: The MLP will be trained using ab initio data that spans the full relevant composition range (e.g., equiatomic or near-equiatomic mixtures common in high-entropy alloys) and temperature range from just below to above the melting temperature. Thermodynamic integration tests (using TOR-TILD methodology) will be performed under the same conditions as in the baseline EAM approach, ensuring identical composition, pressure, and temperature settings.
generation.structural_mediator: The many-body interaction terms encoded in the machine-learning potential capture the local and medium-range chemical order as well as the disordered liquid environments, serving as the mediator by bridging the configurational diversity between the ab initio target and the reference system.
generation.mechanism: Because the MLP is trained on a diverse set of atomic configurations including those typical in the ab initio liquid, it offers a more faithful description of both short- and mid-range ordering, resulting in better phase-space overlap. This improved overlap reduces the discontinuities in the thermodynamic integration path compared to the more rigid and less adaptable EAM models used in TOR-TILD.
generation.predicted_outcome: A lower free-energy integration path mismatch is expected, with the free-energy differences obtained via thermodynamic integration using the MLP showing much closer agreement to direct ab initio calculations than those based on conventional EAM potentials. The hypothesis predicts a substantial reduction in mismatches (potentially on the order of magnitude indicated by analogous elemental and binary system studies), though the exact improvement factor remains uncertain.
generation.baseline: The baseline is the current state where TOR-TILD employs standard EAM references that do not capture the full diversity of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
generation.boundary: This intervention applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys (systems with at least four distinct elements) near and at their high melting temperatures, where both solid and liquid phases are examined. The method is bounded to cases where high-quality ab initio data is available for training the MLP.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the exact quantitative reduction in the integration path mismatch, as it depends on the quality and range of the ab initio data used to train the MLP and on the specific alloy system. The order-of-magnitude improvement observed in simpler systems may not uniformly translate to all high-entropy alloys.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermodynamic integration on the same high-entropy alloy system using two references: (a) the conventional EAM as used in TOR-TILD and (b) the newly developed MLP trained on ab initio data spanning the solid and liquid configurations. Both simulations are conducted under identical temperature, pressure, and composition conditions. Compare the free-energy differences and phase-space overlap metrics obtained from both methods.
measurements: Metrics quantifying phase-space overlap (e.g., probability distributions of key structural descriptors)
Structural correlation functions characterizing local order in both phases
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLP-based integration does not yield a statistically significant reduction in the thermodynamic integration path mismatch (i.e., the free-energy difference is not closer to the direct ab initio benchmark) or if phase-space overlap metrics remain comparable to those from the EAM-based approach, then the hypothesis is falsified.
